name: Jeshua
overview: Jeshua was a male Levite who returned to Judah following the Babylonian captivity. He was the son of Jozadak and played a significant role in the restoration of worship by helping to build the altar. His return marks an important moment in the reestablishment of the community in Judah after exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshua means "y-h-v-h saves," reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to God's saving power. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 2:2 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Jeshua as the son of Jozadak and infers that Joiakim was his father. He is also noted as a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the broader covenant lineage of Israel.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshua's significance lies in his role as a Levite who actively participated in the post-exilic restoration of worship in Judah. As the son of Jozadak, he inherited a priestly heritage and contributed to rebuilding the altar, which was central to reestablishing proper worship practices. His return from Babylonian captivity symbolizes the faithfulness of God in preserving His people and their worship.
